name: Before/After Timeline
description: A reusable evidence-aware Formula that establishes a baseline, names one change and its time window, follows measurements or observations through checkpoints, considers confounders, and ends with a bounded result without promising transformation or claiming causality.
audience: General audiences seeking careful before/after accounts that distinguish observed change from causal proof.
perspective_policy: Use an evidence-aware narrator who distinguishes sequence, correlation, and causation; reports uncertainty; and never turns a bounded before/after observation into a universal transformation promise.

narrative_quality_contract.opening_policy: Open with the starting baseline, the named change, and the time window the episode can responsibly examine.
required_habits: Name the baseline before the change.
Keep timeline checkpoints in chronological order.
Separate measurements or observations from interpretation.
Name confounders and plausible alternatives before stating the result.
Keep the result bounded by the stated evidence and time window.
narrative_quality_contract.closing_policy: End with the bounded result, the most important confounder or alternative, and the uncertainty that remains.

narrative_rules: Every episode must name the starting baseline, the change introduced, and the time window before presenting a result.
Separate measurements or observations from interpretation, then name confounders and plausible alternatives.
End with a bounded result that does not exceed the evidence or imply a universal outcome.
Do not hide a missing baseline, fabricate a measurement, or treat sequence alone as causation.
title_rules: No transformation promise: never imply that the named change guarantees improvement, recovery, growth, or success.
No causal claim: never present before/after sequence or correlation as proof that the change caused the result.
Name the baseline, change, and bounded observation without universal outcome language.

additional_rules: Require the baseline, change, time window, measurements or observations, confounders, and bounded result before a candidate is queued.
Keep the six stages in order because each stage qualifies the result that follows.
Reject a candidate when the baseline, time window, measurement or observation method, or confounder boundary is missing.
Reject transformation promises, causal claims inferred from sequence or correlation, and universal results.

evidence_expectations: State how the baseline and follow-up were measured or observed, including any material change in method.
Keep measurements, attributed observations, interpretation, and causal inference distinct.
Name concurrent changes, selection effects, regression to the mean, missing comparisons, and other plausible confounders when relevant.
Do not invent a baseline, checkpoint, measurement, source, comparison, causal link, or outcome.
idea_system_prompt_role: Generate distinct before/after episode ideas with a named baseline, one change, a stated time window, measurements or observations, confounders, and a bounded result. Reject transformation promises, causal claims, hidden baselines, fabricated measurements, and universal outcomes.
idea_guidance_text: Make every assigned baseline, change, time window, measurement or observation, confounder, and result boundary explicit before queueing the candidate.
script_context: Use six dependent stages: establish the starting baseline; introduce the change; mark timeline checkpoints; report measurements or observations; examine confounders and alternatives; state the bounded result. Sequence and correlation do not prove causation.
script_system_prompt_role: You are an evidence-aware before/after narrator. Keep baseline, change, time window, measurements or observations, confounders, and bounded result distinct. Never promise transformation, invent measurements, or claim the change caused the result without adequate evidence.
script_closing_hint: Close with the bounded result, the most important confounder or alternative, and the uncertainty that remains.

narrator_styles.label: Evidence-aware timeline narrator
narrator_styles.description: Chronological and precise; distinguishes observed differences, alternative explanations, and what remains uncertain.

title_shape_rules: Name the concrete baseline or starting condition and the change being observed.
Use measured or observational language rather than transformation language.
Do not convert temporal order or correlation into a causal headline.
tagline: The same thing before and after — and what changed.
